key_insight: FrozenLGP makes divide-and-conquer QAOA work on dense or highly connected graphs by freezing a minimal set of obstructing vertices and absorbing their effects into the remaining Ising model.
engineering_relevance: It provides a topology-robust preprocessing layer for distributed quantum optimization, extending QAOA to larger problem instances on near-term hardware with fewer entangling-gate demands.
method: Detect when standard graph partitioning fails on a target instance.
Compute a minimum vertex cut via max-flow, then freeze those qubits classically.
Fold removed interaction energies into linear bias terms on neighboring active qubits.
evidence_signal: Across graphs up to 10,000 vertices and multiple topology families, FrozenLGP achieved 100% decomposition coverage versus 4.6% for the standard baseline on high-connectivity cases, while preserving MaxCut quality and improving noise robustness.
watch_item: The approach depends on a classical min-cut/freeze step and bias reparameterization, so its practical cost and performance may still depend on solver overhead and how accurately the frozen contributions are integrated.
paper_title: Adaptive Qubit Freezing Enables Robust Graph Partitioning for Divide-and-Conquer QAOA
